spec.full_target: Let n,m be positive integers, u:R^n×(0,∞)→R^m jointly smooth and q a unit vector. Assume |u|=1, u_tt−Δ_xu=a u, and u=q outside compact spatial sets uniformly on compact time intervals. Define e=|u_t|²+Σ|∂_xj u|² and E=∫e dx. Prove e integrable, E differentiable, E'=0 for all r>0.
spec.conclusion: For every r>0, e(·,r) is Lebesgue integrable, E is differentiable at r, and E'(r)=0.

argument.text: Fix r>0, J=[r/2,3r/2], and choose compact C from H003. For every s∈J, u(·,s)=q on the open complement of C. Smoothness implies every first and higher derivative in x and t vanishes there; consequently e and e_t at each fixed s are continuous and supported in C, hence compactly supported. M001 applies with X=ℝⁿ, Lebesgue measure and V=ℝ, since Euclidean opens are Borel measurable and Lebesgue measure is finite on compact sets. Thus e(·,s), e_t(·,s), and all continuous compactly supported scalar fields below are integrable; E(s) is the ordinary finite Lebesgue integral. C×J is compact by M005, and e_t is continuous on it, so M004 gives uniform continuity. Apply M006 with α=ℝⁿ, μ=Lebesgue, 𝕜=ℝ, E=ℝ, x₀=r, s=(r/2,3r/2), F(τ)(x)=e(x,τ), F'(τ)(x)=e_t(x,τ). The neighborhood inclusion holds; F(τ) is strongly measurable because it is continuous, and F(r) integrable by M001; F'(r) is strongly measurable. Continuity on compact C×J gives a finite bound K for |e_t| there. Set b=K·1_C; C is compact measurable of finite measure, so b is integrable. Outside C the derivative vanishes, and on C it is bounded by K; hence |F'(τ)(x)|≤b(x) for τ∈s. Smoothness gives the required HasDerivAt in τ for every x and τ. All M006 hypotheses are now checked, yielding E differentiable at r and E'(r)=∫e_t(x,r)dx. For the later coordinate argument choose L bounding C: each coordinate projection of C is compact and therefore bounded; the finitely many coordinate bounds have a common finite maximum. The box [-L,L]^n contains C. C and J compact give C×J compact by M005; these are proved compactness facts, not properties granted by the witness declarations.

For fixed r and each j define g_j(x)=u_t(x,r)·u_{x_j}(x,r). The factors and their derivatives vanish outside C, so g_j and ∂_j g_j are smooth and compactly supported; M001 proves their integrability. Product differentiation gives ∂_j g_j=(∂_j u_t)·u_{x_j}+u_t·u_{x_jx_j}, with each dot product the finite sum over m components. For fixed other coordinates y, z↦g_j(x(y,z)) is smooth and zero for |z|>L. Apply M007 with u(z)=g_j(x(y,z)), v(z)=1, u′(z)=∂_j g_j(x(y,z)), v′(z)=0, endpoints −L,L. Both functions are continuous on the closed interval, differentiable in its interior, and their derivatives are interval-integrable because they are continuous there; M007 therefore gives ∫_{−L}^L ∂_j g_j dz=g_j(L)−g_j(−L)=0. The derivative vanishes outside this interval, so its whole-line integral on each coordinate fiber is zero. For n=1 the other-coordinate space is the singleton ℝ⁰. The coordinate-permuted derivative is continuous compactly supported, hence product-integrable by M001. Coordinate permutation preserves Lebesgue measure (it permutes orthonormal coordinate axes); the factor Lebesgue measures are σ-finite, hence S-finite, and ℝ is real normed, so M003 identifies its whole-space integral with the iterated integral, equal to zero. Thus ∫∂_j g_j=0 and ∫(∂_j u_t)·u_{x_j}=−∫u_t·u_{x_jx_j}; all fields are integrable by M001. Differentiate the exact Frobenius energy formula: e_t=2u_t·u_{tt}+2Σ_j u_{x_j}·∂_j u_t. Finite sums commute with integration. Summing the integration-by-parts identities and using Δ_xu=Σ_j u_{x_jx_j} gives E′(r)=2∫u_t·(u_{tt}−Δ_xu). Differentiating H001 gives 2u·u_t=0, hence u·u_t=0. At the same point H002 supplies a scalar a with u_{tt}−Δ_xu=a u. Inner product with u_t gives u_t·(u_{tt}−Δ_xu)=a(u_t·u)=0. The zero integrand is integrable, so E′(r)=0. No regularity of a is used; r>0 was arbitrary.

K·1_C is integrable: C is compact measurable of finite Lebesgue measure and the function is bounded with support in C.
